subject.title: [Feature]: Add TTL/Expiry for Delivery Queue Messages

question: Should outbound delivery recovery add an operator-configurable TTL, and if so what default behavior and expired-entry action should be the supported public contract?
rationale: The fix changes public config/default behavior and persisted queue semantics, and root policy treats config/default and delivery-state changes as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Opt-in TTL with failed-entry retention
options.body: Preserve current no-TTL behavior by default, add a documented `messages.delivery` TTL, and move expired entries to failed/dead-letter state with logging.

options.title: Bounded default TTL
options.body: Ship a default max age for all users, accepting that upgrades may stop replaying older pending entries without operator opt-in.

options.title: Fold into broader lifecycle work
options.body: Defer this issue until a larger delivery lifecycle policy owns outbound expiry, inbound freshness, and queue cleanup together.

recommendation.title: Opt-in TTL with failed-entry retention
recommendation.body: Preserve current no-TTL behavior by default, add a documented `messages.delivery` TTL, and move expired entries to failed/dead-letter state with logging.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already provided maintainer review direction on this issue and has recent history in the current delivery-queue split.
